claims.observed_value: ADHP dual-tree preprocessing complexity is O(K * m * log n)
claims.evidence: Reverse Dijkstra run K times from destination t; each pass on graph with n vertices and m edges using a binary heap requires O(m log n) time. Precomputing K dual trees takes K * O(m log n) = O(K * m log n). Proven in docs/COMPLEXITY_ANALYSIS.md Section 2.
claims.assumptions: Assumes binary heap priority queue. With Fibonacci heaps, bound is O(K(m + n log n)).

claims.expected_value: ADHP search phase complexity is O(|F| * m * log n)
claims.observed_value: ADHP search phase complexity is O(|F| * m * log n)
claims.evidence: Search expands non-dominated path labels. In worst case, |F| Pareto labels are extracted from the priority queue, each relaxing at most m/n edges in O(log(|F| * n)). Bounded by O(|F| * m log n) (Carlyle & Wood 2008). Proven in docs/COMPLEXITY_ANALYSIS.md Section 3.
claims.assumptions: |F| is the number of Pareto non-dominated labels generated in search, which can be exponential in the worst case on pathological graphs (Hansen 1980).

claims.expected_value: Martins search complexity is O(|F| * m * log n)
claims.observed_value: Martins search complexity is O(|F| * m * log n)
claims.evidence: Standard Martins multi-criteria label setting (Martins 1984); label dominance checks across all non-dominated path prefixes bounded by |F| * m log n.
claims.assumptions: Zero preprocessing overhead; unguided label exploration suffers severe combinatorial expansion on dense graphs.

claims.expected_value: Dumitrescu-Boland search complexity is O(W * m * log n)
claims.observed_value: Dumitrescu-Boland search complexity is O(W * m * log n)
claims.evidence: Pseudo-polynomial dynamic programming / label setting bounded by integer resource budget W; with 1D distance bounds dc and dw, search expands at most W labels per vertex, giving O(W * m log n) worst-case time (Dumitrescu & Boland 2003).
claims.assumptions: Requires non-negative integer edge weights and integer resource budget W.
